PullRequest.Title: Shard Windows tests as they're too slow to run 20x in one job

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The top-level parameter comment explicitly supports shortening `iterations` for manual debugging, and the default shard list, parity predicate placement, and common-template boundaries are all statically visible. For `[1]`, the odd job has one test and the even job has none, but both instantiate all setup tasks. Exact artifact sizes and wall-clock duration are unknown, affecting severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one extra Windows agent job, three pipeline-artifact downloads, three archive extractions, one Key Vault call, and one Electron/Playwright setup invocation per short run whose iterations occupy only one parity
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The redundant cost is one full integration-job setup whenever the supplied iteration set contains only odd or only even values; it dominates the intended work as the manual iteration count shrinks, reaching a 2:1 job/setup fan-out for a single test iteration.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive I/O and reduced shared CI throughput
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous integration path always instantiated one job, so a shortened one-iteration debugging run downloaded and extracted each of the three artifacts and initialized the toolchain exactly once before running that test.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every enabled Windows integration invocation now creates two jobs before considering which iteration values belong to either shard. The common template therefore runs both jobs' setup even when one shard receives no test step.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 108 wraps the integration test-job template in a fixed `each shard in parameters.integrationShards` loop whose default is `[odd, even]`; the parity condition is applied only inside `testSteps`, after both jobs have already executed common setup.
Findings.Title: Skip empty shards for shortened debug runs
Findings.Impact: A one-iteration Windows integration debugging run allocates a second Windows agent and repeats all artifact, filesystem, secret-service, and tool-download setup for a job that runs no tests. This creates avoidable network/filesystem I/O and consumes shared CI capacity; the stage must also wait for that empty shard job to finish.
Findings.Evidence: `product-smoke-flaky.yml` documents that `iterations` may be shortened for manual debugging. With a realistic value such as `[1]`, line 108 still expands both `odd` and `even` jobs; only line 143 filters test steps. Before reaching that filter, each common test job downloads the repo, app, and server pipeline artifacts, extracts all three archives, selects Node, calls Azure Key Vault, and runs the Electron/Playwright download command. Thus the one-test scenario now performs six artifact downloads and two complete setup sequences instead of three downloads and one setup sequence, while the even shard executes no test.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the two shards for the default long run, but use the original single-job path for short iteration lists (for example, up to the per-job capacity) or derive/condition the shard jobs so a parity with no assigned iterations is not instantiated.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Twenty intentionally repeated, subprocess-heavy Windows integration runs were serialized in one Azure job, so aggregate duration scaled linearly past the fixed 300-minute job deadline.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: The default Windows integration job could not finish its 20 iterations before Azure's 300-minute timeout, truncating scheduled flaky-test runs.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The change partitions the 20 Windows integration invocations into odd and even jobs that run concurrently after the shared build, reducing the integration critical path from roughly 400–480 minutes to roughly 200–240 minutes plus setup and keeping each shard within its explicit 360-minute job timeout.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base template placed every value from the top-level default 20-entry `iterations` list into one Windows integration job (`each i in parameters.iterations` at base line 128). Each iteration invokes `scripts/test-integration.bat`, and the changed comments document ~20–24 minutes per Windows iteration while the common job timeout was 300 minutes. Thus the scheduled twice-daily default path required roughly 400–480 serial minutes in a job capped at 300 minutes. The added shard loop at line 108 creates exactly two jobs and the parity predicate assigns each default iteration to one of them, preserving 20 test invocations while reducing each job to 10 serial invocations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Twice-daily default Windows flaky integration run
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shared Windows build completes first. The odd and even integration jobs then run concurrently, and the Windows stage waits for both. Each shard performs setup followed by 10 serial integration subprocesses. At the documented ~24 minutes per iteration, the tests dominate each shard's critical path and reduce the prior roughly 400–480-minute serial path to roughly 200–240 minutes plus setup, within the new 360-minute timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the shared built workspace, packaged application, and packaged server into each shard workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six pipeline-artifact downloads total: repo, app, and server once in each of two shards; before the diff there were three total in one integration job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One integration job downloaded each of the three artifacts once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three downloads must complete in each shard before that shard can test, so the slower setup contributes to the max of the two shard paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract repo.zip, app.zip, and server.zip into each agent workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six archive extractions total, three per shard; before the diff there were three total.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The single integration job extracted the three archives once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each shard must extract all archives before Node/tool setup and tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve the GitHub token and run npm-based Electron/Playwright installation in each job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two Key Vault task calls and two Electron/Playwright setup invocations, versus one of each before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The single integration job performed each setup operation once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both operations precede tests in each shard. They execute concurrently across shards but are serial prerequisites within a shard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch scripts/test-integration.bat against the packaged Electron app and server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Twenty integration test subprocess invocations remain; parity assigns 10 to each default shard instead of 20 serial invocations in one job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same 20 invocations ran serially in one job and exceeded the prior 300-minute job timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These are the dominant critical-path work. Two-way execution shortens elapsed stage latency while preserving aggregate test count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish per-shard crash and log directories as pipeline artifacts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four output artifact publications total (crash and log artifacts per shard), versus two from the former job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One integration job published one crash artifact and one log artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication occurs as job output after test steps and must complete for each job, but is small relative to 10 documented long-running test iterations unless logs are unusually large.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The default 20-entry `iterations` list is partitioned by parity into two effective groups of 10; there is no duplication of test iterations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly two Windows integration jobs are generated by the default `[odd, even]` shard list. Each job serializes its 10 assigned iterations; aggregate integration-test subprocess concurrency rises from one to two. Unit and smoke jobs remain independently parallel as before. No repository-level limiter is present, so actual execution can be constrained only by the external Azure Windows agent pool.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Azure jobs have separate workspaces, so the second shard cannot reuse the first shard's extracted artifacts or local Electron/Playwright files. Pipeline-artifact downloads are independently fetched per job; any service-side or package-cache warmth may reduce bytes but does not coalesce the two setup sequences. There is no changed application cache or negative-cache path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: template expansion, default cardinality, serial per-job step ordering, subprocess count, and all duplicated boundaries are explicit in the YAML.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact artifact sizes, setup duration, cache warmth, and Azure pool contention are not available. Those uncertainties affect the extra resource cost, not the established two-way concurrency or the documented timeout arithmetic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression finding for the default path. The bounded duplication of setup and artifact I/O is an intentional tradeoff that halves the dominant serial test critical path and prevents a demonstrated timeout. The prior regression and its introducing commit were recorded with report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Short manual Windows integration debugging run
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the shared build, both fixed shard jobs are stage dependencies. For a one-item list such as `[1]`, the odd job performs setup plus one roughly 24-minute test while the even job performs the same setup and no test. The active job will often remain the dominant path, but the stage still cannot complete before the empty job; independently, the empty job consumes I/O and agent capacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize repo, app, and server in both the active and empty shard workspaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six artifact downloads and six archive extractions for one test iteration, versus three downloads and three extractions in the former single job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A shortened manual run used one job and materialized the artifacts once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Three downloads and extractions in the empty shard provide no test progress; the stage nevertheless waits for that job.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize secrets and test runtimes in both fixed shards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two Key Vault calls and two Electron/Playwright setup invocations for one test, versus one of each before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One setup sequence served the shortened iteration list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The empty shard's calls cannot advance a test and consume remote-service and agent resources; they can delay stage completion if their job finishes after the active shard or queues behind constrained capacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the one manually requested Windows integration iteration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One integration-test subprocess invocation in the active shard and zero in the other; aggregate test count is unchanged from the requested one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The one subprocess ran after a single job setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The sole test remains on the critical path; sharding provides no test parallelism benefit for this input.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Manual `iterations` values containing only one parity, especially the documented shortened one-iteration debugging case. Redundant setup is fixed at one full job and becomes proportionally larger as requested test count approaches one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two jobs are instantiated even though effective test cardinality is one and only one parity has work. There is no conditional suppression of the empty shard; actual simultaneous execution depends on Azure pool availability.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The two shard jobs have isolated workspaces. An empty shard still cannot reuse the active shard's artifact files or local tool setup, and no condition prevents its common-template steps. External package caches may be warm but do not eliminate job allocation, task calls, archive extraction, or setup command execution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the top-level YAML explicitly advertises shortened lists for manual debugging, the fixed two-shard expansion occurs outside the parity-filtered test steps, and `[1]` deterministically leaves the even shard empty.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Artifact byte counts, setup time, and frequency of manual shortened runs are unknown. The exact duplicated boundary cardinality and empty-job reachability are certain; uncertainty therefore supports low severity rather than omission.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity boundary fan-out: the diff doubles job setup and artifact I/O while providing no parallel test work when the shortened list occupies one parity. Finding submitted at the added shard loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Other flaky-test suites using the common test-job template
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Linux/macOS test jobs and Windows unit/smoke jobs retain the same one-job-per-suite structure and 300-minute deadline. The parameter substitution is resolved at template expansion and adds no runtime work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: All iteration counts for Linux/macOS unit, integration, and smoke jobs and Windows unit/smoke jobs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged for all common-template consumers except the explicitly sharded Windows integration caller.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, cache lifetime, or cache access changes. Existing consumers omit the new parameter and receive its 300-minute default, exactly matching the prior hard-coded timeout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: repository search found every common-template call site, and the new timeout parameter defaults to the exact previous literal value.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: all call sites were inspected and only Windows integration passes a non-default timeout or adds job fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The common timeout parameterization preserves prior behavior and introduces no boundary, allocation, or concurrency change for these callers.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all relevant template callers. Submitted one low-severity boundary-fan-out finding for empty shards in shortened manual runs. The default two-way Windows integration sharding is a concrete latency/timeout fix, not a regression; its introducing commit was recorded for regression learning. No other changed path adds unbounded concurrency, retention, eager application work, or altered cache behavior.
